newsitem.title: GERMANY: Higher costs, provisions hit Lufthansa in 96.
newsitem.headline: Higher costs, provisions hit Lufthansa in 96.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday that its 1996 operating profit was just below its pre-tax profit figure of almost 700 marks.

In a statement issued in response to an unpublished article in the German business magazine Capital, Lufthansa said that its 1996 figures would not match those seen in 1995, but that losses would be "far below" those alleged in the article.
This confirmed prognoses made by the company last week, when they said 1996 earnings would be lower than the previous year. It is due to report its 1996 results on May 7.
The group said that higher fuel costs in the second half of 1996 led to increased charges at 320 million marks.
This combined with a one-off charge of 110 million marks in additional pension provisions, resulting in higher charges of 430 million marks over the year.
"Without these items Lufthansa would have reported clearly higher earnings on an operational and consolidated basis," Lufthansa said in the statement.

"The figures cited by Capital are wrong," Lufthansa said, referring to the report, to be published on Friday, which claimed that the economic situation at the airline was worse than Lufthansa itself had claimed.
"Lufthansa is totally against the use of cosmetic accounting. The annual results will be examined by auditors as in any other public company," Lufthansa said.
Lufthansa shares were down 29 pfennigs, or 1.28 percent, at 22.30 marks in post-bourse trade.
